intended_object: The modal logic of a class C of Kripke frames: the set of formulas that are valid on every frame in C, Log(C) = {φ | ∀ F ∈ C, F ⊨ φ}. Inferred from the name and the body.
explanation: `C ⊧ φ` is the library's `ValidOnFrameClass`, which is defined as `∀ {F}, F ∈ C → F ⊧ φ`. A formula is valid on a frame when it holds at every world under every valuation. So `{φ | C ⊧ φ}` is exactly the standard logic of a frame class. Formulas use the library's fixed type of propositional variables (`Formula ℕ`), which is a standard choice of a countable set of atoms and is used throughout the framework, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no modal logic or Kripke semantics, so there is no counterpart.
